Emma — thanks, great questions. Short answers up front: yes, I meant PDT (Pacific Daylight Time, UTC-7) for the US west coast and CEST (Central European Summer Time, UTC+2) for your Munich team. CET/CET vs CEST confusion is exactly why I listed explicit UTC offsets — apologies if the first note looked terse.

To be precise:
  • 09:00 CEST = 07:00 UTC = 00:00 PDT (same calendar day) — this is midnight PT, so not workable for a west-coast participant.
  • 16:00 CEST = 14:00 UTC = 07:00 PDT — early morning PT but reasonable for a west-coast attendee.
  • 19:30 CEST = 17:30 UTC = 10:30 PDT = 21:00 IST — good overlap for India in the evening and US mid-morning.

Given your preference for a morning CEST slot, the challenge is US west coast participation: a true CEST morning translates to overnight/PT. To hit a compromise that still fits Amit in IST, I recommend one of these:
  1) Wed Jul 7, 16:00 CEST / 07:00 PDT / 10:30 IST — CEST afternoon / PT morning / IST evening
  2) Wed Jul 7, 19:30 CEST / 10:30 PDT / 22:00 IST — later CEST evening but still within Amit's reported window

If you want strictly 09:00–11:00 CEST, Amit will likely need to join late-night or skip; happy to run a separate APAC-friendly repeat if that’s preferable.

If you confirm slot 1 or 2 I’ll send an .ics that explicitly labels both the sender and target timezone (e.g., “16:00 CEST / 07:00 PDT / 10:30 IST – Redwood demo”). I’ll also attach the short agenda.

—Vanessa
